instructions: You are the assistant of the EDev-Vision Okavango Delta flood app. Answer ONLY from the data and facts in this document. If the answer is not here, say you do not have that data. Quote numbers with their unit, date and source layer. Keep three sources apart and never add or average them: (1) NISAR L-band radar, 2026, open water AND flooded vegetation; (2) Landsat optical history, 1984-2025, open water only; (3) modelled river discharge and headwater rainfall, the drivers. Satellites measure the AREA of water, not its depth, volume or quality: never state how much water is drinkable. Mention uncertainty when it applies (uncalibrated thresholds, low-coverage years, model not gauge). NISAR km2 and Landsat km2 measure different things: never put them side by side or say one is larger. To judge whether 2026 was a big year use ONLY the river-discharge rank; Landsat has no 2026 value. Read each number from its own column; do not mix open water with flooded vegetation. If asked about the future (2026-2030), use future_projection only: give the median and the 80% range in km2 of Landsat-type open water, say it is a statistical projection of our own algorithm (rain after April 2026 has not fallen yet, so 2027-2030 are uncertain), and never present it as certain or as NISAR flooded vegetation. If asked why a past year was unusually wet or dry, use future_projection.outlier_years and contributions. Never show field names or raw level numbers from this document (write 'far below normal', not '-2'; write 'Landsat', not a key name). Causes are associations, not proof: say 'went together with', not 'was caused by'. Answer in the user's language, in plain words for non-experts, in at most 120 words. Plain sentences only: no tables, no headings, no citation marks or brackets.

background_facts.fact: The flood is driven by rain that falls months earlier in the Angolan highlands and travels down the Okavango River; it reaches the Delta in the local dry season.
Mean annual input (river plus local rain) is about 16 km3; roughly 96-98% returns to the atmosphere by evapotranspiration and only about 2% leaves as surface outflow towards Maun.
background_facts.source: Okavango water-balance literature (EGU2011-13435; Jao/Boro outflow modelling study)

background_facts.fact: Open water is dark in radar (mirror reflection). Flooded vegetation is bright in HH (double bounce between water and stems). L-band penetrates the canopy; optical sensors and shorter radar wavelengths mostly do not.

Why the water shrinks within a year: river inflow peaks around February-April, the flood wave takes months to cross the flat Delta, and after it passes the inflow keeps falling while evapotranspiration and seepage into the sand remove the water. It is a normal seasonal retreat, not a sign of a drying Delta.
background_facts.source: discharge_2026_monthly_m3s in this document; water-balance literature

background_facts.fact: HYPOTHESIS (ours, not proven): flooded vegetation peaks weeks after open water because the flood first fills the open channels and lagoons and only later spreads sideways into the vegetated floodplains.
background_facts.source: EDev-Vision interpretation of the NISAR series

nisar_2026.what: NISAR L-band radar, L2 GCOV, 80 m, one track/frame/pass, so differences between dates are real surface change.
nisar_2026.noise_filter: Multitemporal speckle filter (Quegan & Yu 2001), 5x5 local window, over all 10 dates; then classified pixels with no same-class neighbour are removed.
caveats: Thresholds are physical rules, not calibrated on the ground: a consistent relative index and a LOWER bound, not an absolute area. The seasonal shape is more reliable than the level.
The AOI and one radar frame do not cover the whole Delta.
The last date is a VALIDATED product, the rest PROVISIONAL; its small rise in open water may be a calibration step.

optical_history.what: Landsat optical (Digital Earth Africa WOfS annual), OPEN water only, km2 of the AOI wet in >=10% of cloud-free looks in that calendar year.
optical_history.low_coverage_meaning: fewer than 8 looks: a lower bound, the flood may simply have been missed
optical_history.caveat: Misses water under vegetation; never compare its level with NISAR's.

drivers.what: Peak monthly river discharge near Mohembo (GloFAS MODEL, not a gauge) and Nov-Apr rainfall in the Angolan headwaters (NASA POWER, three points).

findings.how_2026_compares: By modelled peak monthly inflow, 2026 (807.9 m3/s) ranks 14 of 30 years (1997-2026): an average year. Caution: this river model is unreliable in some years; it shows 2025 as weak although Landsat mapped a normal-sized flood that year.

causes_and_people_by_year.what: Level of each cause per year, -2 (pushes towards a small flood) to +2 (towards a large flood), against the 1991-2020 normal. people = residents within 5 km of that year's Landsat open water (2020 population held fixed). Causes are associations, not proof.
causes_and_people_by_year.sentences_2026: The rainy season came with a neutral Pacific (index -0.4). Rain in the Angolan highlands was 14% above normal (1057 mm). Modelled river inflow peaked at 808 m3/s, rank 14 of 30 years since 1997. Rain over the Delta itself was 38% above normal (781 mm). Flood-season days were 0.9 C cooler than normal.

documented_events.title: Floods displace families
documented_events.text: Floods on the Okavango, Zambezi and Chobe displaced 430 people and submerged eight villages. In Ngamiland 61 hectares of ploughed fields went under water and lodges at Sepopa were flooded.

documented_events.title: Largest floods in recent memory
documented_events.text: Between 2010 and 2012 the Delta saw some of its largest floods in recent memory; channels and lagoons dry for decades refilled and water reached Lake Ngami.
documented_events.source: okavango.com (travel guide, not a scientific source)

documented_events.title: The flood did not arrive
documented_events.text: Water sources across Ngamiland dried up, leaving communities, livestock and wildlife in a dire situation. Fishermen and mokoro polers lost their income and farmers lost cattle.

documented_events.title: The Delta springs back to life
documented_events.text: The flood returned and was expected to reach the Thamalakane River at Maun in mid-May, restoring water for farming, fishing and mokoro tourism.

documented_events.title: Hippos stranded near Maun
documented_events.text: During an El Nino drought the Thamalakane River dried up and herds of hippos were stuck in drying pools near Maun; wildlife officials warned they were in danger of dying.

caveats: Causes are associations, not proof: a year can be wet for reasons not listed here, and last year's water carries over.
River inflow is a hydrological model. It disagrees with the mapped water in some years (for example 2025).
Population is held at its 2020 distribution in every year, so the change between years comes from the water, not from growth. Living near water is not the same as being flooded or helped.
Events are from news reports and a travel guide; they are illustrations, not a complete record.

plain: The radar's noise floor is steady across all ten dates, so the seasonal change is not an instrument effect.
Open water is clearly above the noise in HH but only about 2 dB above it in HV. Open water is therefore mapped mainly by HH; its HV value is mostly instrument noise.
NASA did not subtract thermal noise in these products, so very dark surfaces read slightly brighter than they are. This does not affect the bright flooded-vegetation class.
NASA's 'mask' layer marks samples that were not fully focused as invalid; these are the same edge-strip pixels our noise-floor rule already removes.

future_projection.what: RSynthesis estimation engine v2.1, our own algorithm: yearly open water in the study area (Landsat type, km2) and a probability map (0 to 1 per 120 m pixel), 2026-2030.
future_projection.how: Stage 1 (how much): Equal mixture of 4 robust Bayesian models on a Box-Cox scale; core causes: Rain in the Angolan highlands (Nov-Apr), Calendar year (slow change); optional causes: Rain over the Delta (Nov-Apr), El Nino / La Nina (Dec-Feb ocean index). Student-t errors, low-coverage years as lower bounds, Gibbs sampling. Cause screening is repeated inside each validation fold. Stage 2 (where): a Bayesian logistic regression for each pixel places the water. For future years with unknown causes, the algorithm samples all causes together from a past year, preserving their correlations.
future_projection.dropped_causes: Tested but not retained in the final model: Flood-season heat (May-Oct), Last year's rain in the Angolan highlands, river inflow (gauge and GloFAS), where the rain fell
future_projection.trend: With the causes held at a normal year, open water in the study area falls about 14.5 km2 per year (posterior z = -2.64); Angolan rain itself shows no significant trend (t = 0.82). Possible reasons are not separated yet: heat, water moving between Delta channels, upstream use, vegetation closing channels.
future_projection.skill: Yearly area, each year left out: skill 0.583, error 371.2 km2 (the earlier v1: 360.9 km2). Forecasting each year from 2006 from earlier years only: error 498.6 km2 (v1: 380.8). Trained on 1989-2012 and tested on 2013-2025: skill 0.592. Map: Brier skill 0.095 against an average-year map.
rows: known: Angolan rain 1057 mm, Delta rain 781 mm, El Nino index -0.4
caveats: A statistical projection, not a certainty: rain and El Nino after April 2026 are unknown, so 2027-2030 use the causes of past years and the band is wide.
Landsat sees OPEN water only. Water under reeds and papyrus (the NISAR flooded-vegetation class) is not part of this projection.
The downward trend is measured in this study area only. Part of it may be water moving between channels of the Delta, or a long dry phase, rather than a permanent loss.

outlier_years.what: Years the old v1 model (rain + trend, straight line) missed by more than its own typical error, and what v2 says about them.
outlier_years.logic: What most of them share is the rain over the Delta itself (La Nina years tend to bring more of it, El Nino years less): a very wet Delta adds water the highland rain does not explain, a very dry one removes it. Extreme highland rain years also follow a curved, multiplicative law rather than a straight line.
years: 1989: v1 missed by 586 km2, v2 by 273 km2. Explained by a very wet Delta (786 mm of rain on the Delta itself), La Nina (index -1.6).
1998: still not explained (v1 missed by 776 km2, v2 by 535 km2). The measured river inflow was close to what the rain implies (-4%), so the river does not explain it either.
2004: still not explained (v1 missed by 565 km2, v2 by 404 km2). The measured river inflow was 15% above what the rain implies, which matches the miss.
2006: still not explained (v1 missed by 382 km2, v2 by 243 km2). The measured river inflow was close to what the rain implies (-3%), so the river does not explain it either.
2007: still not explained (v1 missed by 611 km2, v2 by 795 km2). The measured river inflow was close to what the rain implies (+0%), so the river does not explain it either.
2010: still not explained (v1 missed by 398 km2, v2 by 586 km2). The measured river inflow was 33% above what the rain implies, which does not match the miss.
2013: still not explained (v1 missed by 444 km2, v2 by 600 km2). The measured river inflow was 16% below what the rain implies, which matches the miss.
2014: v1 missed by 399 km2, v2 by 1 km2. Explained by a very wet Delta (913 mm of rain on the Delta itself), extreme headwater rain (1052 mm) on a multiplicative scale.
2021: v1 missed by 420 km2, v2 by 42 km2. Explained by a very wet Delta (759 mm of rain on the Delta itself), La Nina (index -1.0), extreme headwater rain (595 mm) on a multiplicative scale.
2022: still not explained (v1 missed by 614 km2, v2 by 844 km2). No measured river inflow exists for this year.

contributions.what: km2 each cause added to or removed from a year, against a normal year (exact Shapley split of the v2 estimate).

forecast.verdict: The best predictor beats climatology; a forecast with its interval may be shown.

tests.predictor: Nov-Apr rainfall in the Angolan headwaters

forecast.nisar: NISAR classes are not forecast: ten dates in one season cannot train or validate a model.
